journey.title: Opt out of reminders with the keyboard after choosing Text message
journey.goal: Arrowing from Text message to the opt-out answer hides the mobile number field that no longer applies

functionalJourney.title: Switch reminder channel with a pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Choosing Email then Text message shows only the mobile number field

guards.title: Choose Email with the keyboard and enter an address
guards.goal: Selecting Email reveals the email address field and the address is kept

plan.root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on click events, not on keyboard-driven changes, so selecting a different radio via arrow keys leaves the previously shown conditional field visible.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a change event listener to the radios module and a handler that updates aria-expanded and toggles the conditional content for the changed radio when it has aria-controls, ensuring keyboard selection updates the UI.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation will correctly show/hide conditional fields, ensuring that the appropriate conditional content is hidden when a different radio is selected, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Potential duplicate handling if both click and change events fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent.
If another script also listens for change events on the same radios, there could be unintended side effects, though the change event is standard and unlikely to conflict.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the email radio to the text radio hides the email input and shows the mobile number input.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the text radio to the opt‑out radio hides the mobile number input.
Verify that mouse clicks still correctly show/hide the associated conditional fields.
Verify that the aria‑expanded attribute on each radio reflects its checked state after keyboard selection.

plan.root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on click events via handleClick, which loops through all radios with aria-controls. Keyboard navigation fires change events, but the previous handleChange only processed the target input. When arrowing from a radio with aria-controls (text message) to one without (opt-out), the change event fires on the opt-out radio, so the text message's conditional field remains visible.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a change event listener in init() and a handleChange method that loops through all radios with aria-controls (mirroring handleClick), ensuring keyboard selection updates all conditional fields based on current checked states.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys) will correctly show/hide conditional fields when moving between radio options, including hiding the mobile number field when opting out after selecting Text message, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Duplicate handling if both click and change events fire for the same interaction, but setAttributes is idempotent.
If another script also listens for change events on the same radios, there could be unintended side effects, though the change event is standard and unlikely to conflict.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the email radio to the text radio hides the email input and shows the mobile number input.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the text radio to the opt-out radio hides the mobile number input.
Verify that mouse clicks still correctly show/hide the associated conditional fields.
Verify that the aria-expanded attribute on each radio reflects its checked state after keyboard selection.

plan.root_cause: The radios component only updates conditional visibility on click events within its own module. Keyboard navigation triggers change events on radios in a separate module (opt-out) that shares the same radio group name, but the component instance with conditionals doesn't listen for those change events, so the conditional field remains visible.
plan.repair_strategy: In the radios component's init, detect if the module has any conditional radios (with aria-controls). If so, listen for change events on all radios sharing the same name across the document, and update conditionals in this module whenever any radio in the group changes. Also refactor the click handler into a shared updateConditionals method used by both click and change events.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard navigation (arrow keys) between radio options in the same group, including across separate module containers, will correctly show/hide conditional fields, satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Duplicate updateConditionals calls when both click and change events fire for the same interaction (idempotent, so safe).
If multiple modules with conditionals share the same radio name, each would add change listeners and update their own conditionals, which is desired.
The _govukRadiosChangeListener property on radio elements could conflict with other scripts, but unlikely.
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the email radio to the text radio hides the email input and shows the mobile number input.
Verify that pressing ArrowDown from the text radio to the opt-out radio hides the mobile number input.
Verify that mouse clicks still correctly show/hide the associated conditional fields.
Verify that the aria-expanded attribute on each radio reflects its checked state after keyboard selection.
Verify that the form data for reminder is correctly set to "none" after opting out.
